about: Radio and intercom for chapter 10: the coast home and the walk outside. Time lines hang on the chapter's start (GET 250:00), the walk (GET 254:54) and the chapter's end; the hatch opening, going out, reaching the instrument bay, taking the cassette and coming in are cued by what happens. t = GET (seconds from liftoff). Original lines in the style of the Apollo air-to-ground; not quotes.

lines.text: America, Houston. You are sixteen hours out and right down the middle of the corridor. Three hundred thousand kilometres to go.
Look back there. That little thing is where we were walking.
America, Houston. You are go for the walk outside. Take your time out there.
Cabin pressure coming down. Suits are holding. Everything loose is tied down.
Hatch is open. Out you go. The rail is on your right, all the way down to the bay.
I've got your umbilical. Oh, man. Look at that. The Earth and the Moon, both at once.
That's the instrument bay. The cassette is on top of the mapping camera, the white drum. Pull the pin and lift it out.
America, Houston. We see you have the cassette. Beautiful. Bring it on home.
He's in. Film is stowed. Closing the hatch.
America, Houston. Nice work out there. That is the farthest from home anyone has ever gone for a walk.
America, Houston. Half-way home. The Earth is a good deal bigger down here than it looks to you.
Thirty thousand miles. She's really coming up now.
America, Houston. Your entry corridor is good. Time to stow the cabin and strap in.
